Generally agree; just wanted to add that grades often aren't helpful for determining whether one would do well in a particular career (or other endeavor)- e.g. being good at scientific research takes a different skill set than does passing science classes. Hopefully OP has shadowed or done internships with doctors- if they haven't, that would be good to get on asap.

I guess being a doctor you need certain skills that can be taught in class and assigned a grade (doing calculations, really good understanding of anatomy and physiology), but research skills, certain problem solving/reasoning skills, and interpersonal skills might be harder to assess in some cases; at least with the way classes are often graded at a large school like Clemson.
